title: Waymo crash map shows hundreds of driverless car collisions across LA
source_used: New York Post (analysis by The Basin)
key_facts: Waymo's driverless cars have had 440 reported crashes across Los Angeles County, per Waymo data analysed by The Basin.
Waymo's reported rate fell from 9.4 crashes per million miles (Oct 2024 to Jun 2025) to 5.5 in the following year, a 41% drop.
Much of the drop followed a federal change: since 16 Jun 2025 NHTSA no longer requires reports of certain minor crashes in which another vehicle hits a driverless car.
Waymo's vehicle was stopped or parked in 269 of the 440 crashes; rear-ended 123 times and sideswiped 71 times.
Of 58 crashes with a reported injury, none involved a suspected serious injury or death.
Only 23 of 304 Waymo crashes without reported injuries in the city of Los Angeles had a police report.
quote_evidence: Waymo’s driverless cars have been involved in 440 reported crashes across Los Angeles County, even as the company’s reported collision rate plunged 41%—a drop largely driven by a federal rule change that allowed it to stop reporting certain minor wrecks.
The company’s records show that its vehicles were stopped or parked in 269 of the 440 reported county crashes.
None involved a suspected serious injury or death.
why_it_matters_hint: Falling crash numbers are partly a reporting-rule effect, so they are hard to compare with earlier figures.
notes: NY Post relaying an analysis by The Basin of Waymo-published data.
